headline: Chip-stock rout deepens into Friday pre-market as TSMC capex shock and Netflix miss stack on top of Iran strike risk, pointing to a lower open for a second straight session.
stance: Risk-off into the weekend. Thursday's cash session saw the S&P 500 (PRIOR CASH CLOSE: 7,533.77) drop ~0.5% and the Nasdaq-100 (PRIOR CASH CLOSE: 25,881.95) fall ~1.6% — semis leading the damage for the second day running. Overnight futures are extending: S&P 500 futures -0.7%, Nasdaq-100 futures -1.0%, and Dow futures -0.6% (all OVERNIGHT levels) as Netflix's after-hours miss compounds the chip selloff. The macro backdrop is a tug-of-war: softer CPI/PPI supports a July hold, but six consecutive days of U.S. strikes on Iran keep oil elevated and a September Fed hike on the table at ~51% odds.

news.head: TSMC capex shock triggers semi selloff
news.body: Taiwan Semiconductor beat Q2 estimates with a 77% profit surge, but hiked its 2026 capital-expenditure guidance to $60–64bn from $52–56bn, sparking fears that AI infrastructure spending is outrunning near-term returns — TSM fell 2.3% in Thursday's cash session and a further ~3.6% in Asia Friday.

news.head: Netflix drops 8%+ after hours
news.body: Netflix reported Q2 earnings roughly in line with estimates but guided for a second consecutive quarter of slowing sales growth and said it will cut the frequency of its audience-engagement disclosures, sending shares down more than 8% in extended trading.

news.head: U.S.-Iran strikes continue — day 6
news.body: The U.S. carried out a sixth straight day of strikes on Iranian military targets; Brent crude futures traded above $85/bbl overnight (OVERNIGHT level), with Iran's IRGC threatening to expand the conflict to additional regional energy supply routes.

news.head: Fed officials add hawkish tone
news.body: Hawkish commentary from Federal Reserve officials overnight reinforced uncertainty around a September rate hike, keeping the 10-year yield near its PRIOR CASH CLOSE of 4.57% and limiting any bond-market relief.

news.head: UNH doubles down on earnings beat
news.body: UnitedHealth Group posted a Q2 double beat — topping both adjusted EPS and revenue estimates — and raised its full-year earnings and cash flow outlook, citing better-than-expected medical cost trends.

news.head: Alphabet loses ~$200bn on Gemini delay
news.body: Reports of a delay to the Gemini 3.5 Pro AI rollout erased roughly $200bn in Alphabet market cap after hours, adding to the broader AI-spending skepticism gripping the tape.

news.head: Today's data calendar
news.body: June housing starts, building permits, and industrial production print this morning, alongside the University of Michigan's preliminary July consumer-sentiment survey — a soft sentiment read could reinforce the risk-off tone; earnings from Travelers, Truist Financial, and Fifth Third Bancorp are also due.

implications: Semis are in a classic 'sell the beat' phase: TSMC, ASML, and Micron all printed strong fundamentals this week yet each triggered sector-wide selling — the market is questioning whether ballooning AI capex ($60–64bn at TSMC alone) will generate adequate returns, compressing multiples.

Iran-driven oil prices above $85/bbl (Brent, OVERNIGHT) are the key macro wildcard: they keep the Fed from turning dovish and squeeze consumer real income simultaneously — every additional day of strikes raises the probability of a September rate hike.

Gold (PRIOR CASH CLOSE $3,979.90/oz) is tracking toward a weekly loss exceeding 3%, squeezed between high real rates (2.35%) and the dollar holding near 100.71 — the usual safe-haven bid is being offset by the prospect of tighter Fed policy.

The 10-year/2-year yield curve sits at +41 bps (PRIOR CASH CLOSE) — still positive, signaling no imminent recession signal, but the 10-year at 4.57% is a real headwind for high-multiple tech stocks at a CAPE of 41.9.

The equity risk premium is deeply negative at -2.05%, meaning bonds are more attractively valued than equities on a raw yield comparison — a structural headwind for broad index multiples at current levels.

Positioning: Speculators have almost no bullish bets left in Russell 2000 futures (2nd percentile of 3 years) — a contrarian floor for small-caps. Similarly, 3M SOFR futures show an extended short (2nd percentile) — a contrarian-bullish lean for front-end rates. In FX, British pound speculators are at an extended short (2nd percentile) alongside a modestly extended short in Euro (12th percentile). In commodities, copper speculators are heavily positioned long (94th percentile) — a contrarian warning for copper given the divergence with commercial hedgers. WTI crude specs sit at the 10th percentile — not yet a full contrarian buy signal but leaning that way. Credit positioning is mid-range (HY at 35th percentile) — no crowding signal.

watch.head: Nasdaq-100 futures -1% overnight
watch.body: The Nasdaq-100 (PRIOR CASH CLOSE: 25,881.95) is pointing to a gap lower at the open — watch whether the ~25,600 area holds as buyers step in; a break lower would mark the weakest weekly close since the Iran escalation began.

watch.head: Brent crude $85+ overnight
watch.body: Oil above $85/bbl (OVERNIGHT level vs. PRIOR CASH CLOSE $84.86) is the inflation/Fed hike pressure valve — any diplomatic signal from Tehran or Washington could trigger a sharp reversal and offer relief to equities.

watch.head: UMich sentiment (8:30am ET)
watch.body: July's preliminary consumer sentiment print is the key data release of the morning; a soft reading on inflation expectations could reinforce rate-hike fears and weigh further on cyclicals.

watch.head: Gold holding below $4,000
watch.body: Gold is on track to close the week below its PRIOR CASH CLOSE of $3,979.90 — a sustained break below $3,930 would signal that the Iran/oil inflation narrative has fully overwhelmed the safe-haven bid.

watch.head: USD/JPY at extreme levels
watch.body: The yen (PRIOR CASH CLOSE: 162.36 ¥/$) sits at the 99th percentile of its 3-year range — the most stretched it has been in years — raising the risk of a sharp reversal if the Bank of Japan signals intervention or if risk-off sentiment accelerates.

watch.head: Netflix and SPCX overhang
watch.body: Netflix's 8%+ after-hours drop and SpaceX's continued slide below its $135 IPO price (hitting fresh lows) are poster children for the 'sell the story' dynamic in high-growth names — watch whether they stabilize in regular trading.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: 10-year Treasury yield PRIOR CASH CLOSE 4.57%; 2-year at 4.16% — curve at +41 bps, still positive but the 10-year is pinned by Iran-driven inflation expectations and hawkish Fed commentary.

10-year breakeven inflation (the bond market's inflation forecast) sits at 2.22% (PRIOR CASH CLOSE), reflecting a market that believes the Iran conflict keeps price pressures above the Fed's 2% target for longer.
Real rates (inflation-adjusted yield) at 2.35% (PRIOR CASH CLOSE) — historically high and a structural drag on gold, growth stocks, and leveraged assets.
Fed funds market currently prices a ~90% probability of a July 29 hold, but September hike odds are ~51%, making any oil spike this weekend a potential catalyst for rate repricing.

Financial conditions remain loose overall: the Chicago Fed National Financial Conditions Index at -0.535 and the St. Louis Fed Stress Index at -0.88 both signal easy money despite elevated nominal rates.
4-week commercial paper spread over risk-free rate: 18 bps — no funding-market stress.

Treasury General Account at $756.2bn and bank reserves at $3,142.7bn — system liquidity is ample; overnight reverse-repo usage is essentially zero ($0.1bn), meaning cash has been fully deployed out of the Fed's facility.
sections.positioning: Speculators have almost no bullish bets left in 3M SOFR futures (2nd percentile of 3 years, extended short) — a contrarian-bullish lean for front-end rates, meaning futures are pricing more hike risk than speculators have historically sustained at these levels.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: S&P 500 PRIOR CASH CLOSE 7,533.77; Nasdaq-100 PRIOR CASH CLOSE 25,881.95; Dow PRIOR CASH CLOSE 52,552.97 — all three closed lower Thursday with the Nasdaq-100 the worst performer (-1.6%).
Overnight futures (pre-market ~6am ET): S&P 500 futures -0.7%, Nasdaq-100 futures -1.0%, Dow futures -0.6% — pointing to a lower open Friday.

Semis drove Thursday's selloff: the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 4.3%; Micron -8%, Intel -5.8%, Nvidia -2.4%, AMD -5%+, Broadcom -5% — all on positioning and capex-return fears, not demand weakness.
VIX PRIOR CASH CLOSE 16.73 — fear gauge is calm relative to the magnitude of the chip selloff, suggesting the broad market is treating this as a sector rotation rather than a systemic risk event.

Market breadth is mixed: 59.4% of S&P 500 stocks trade above their 50-day moving average and 65.9% above their 200-day (as of Jul 15) — underpins the view that damage is concentrated in tech/semis, not broad market.

CAPE ratio at 41.9 with a negative equity risk premium (-2.05%) — equities remain expensive on a structural basis; 'buy the dip' works in an earnings-growth regime but is harder to sustain if the Fed hikes in September.
Q2 S&P 500 earnings growth is tracking at ~23.3% year-over-year per analyst estimates — the second consecutive 20%+ quarter — providing fundamental support even as multiples come under pressure.
Alphabet erased ~$200bn in market cap after hours on Gemini 3.5 Pro delay news — a further headwind for Nasdaq at Friday's open.
sections.positioning: Speculators have almost no bullish bets left in Russell 2000 futures (2nd percentile of 3 years, extended short vs. commercials at the opposite extreme) — a contrarian floor; small-caps could outperform large-cap tech if the semi-led selloff continues to drive rotation.

single_name.note: Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM) — world's largest chipmaker; large off-exchange block buying (quiet institutional accumulation) and a burst of unusual options activity flagged in our scan, company insiders have been buying, stock trades above its 200-day line. Despite Thursday's -2.3% cash-session drop on capex fears, fundamentals remain intact (77% Q2 profit growth, AI demand 'extremely robust') — the setup flags squeeze risk with shorts carrying 1.8 days to cover.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: HY-IG spread at 271 bps (as of Jul 15) — high-yield bonds cost 271 bps more than investment-grade to borrow, a mid-range reading; no systemic stress signal.

Investment-grade option-adjusted spread at 79 bps (as of Jul 15) — tight by historical standards, consistent with easy financial conditions and the low FRA-OIS (1 bp) and SOFR-OIS (1 bp) spreads that show no interbank funding stress.

HY/IG ETF price ratio at 1.3471 (PRIOR CASH CLOSE Jul 16) — junk bonds are holding up relative to investment-grade, which means credit markets are not yet sounding an alarm that the equity selloff is a credit event.
Bank credit growth at 5.93% year-over-year (as of Jul 1) and syndicated loan yields at 6.96% — lending is expanding at a healthy pace; no credit-crunch signal.
Senior loan officer survey (SLOOS) shows net 8.1% of banks tightening C&I loan standards and 2% tightening commercial real estate standards (as of Apr 2026) — modest tightening, not alarming.
M2 money supply growing at 5.58% year-over-year (as of May 2026) — monetary fuel is still being added to the system, supporting nominal asset prices.
Term premium at 77.9 bps — investors are demanding more compensation to hold long-duration Treasuries, a headwind for long bonds and a support for the dollar.

single_name.note: Scorpio Tankers (STNG) — oil product tanker operator; large off-exchange block buying and a burst of unusual options activity, 2 insider buying rules fired, stock trades above its 200-day line. Elevated energy prices from Strait of Hormuz tensions support tanker day rates — signal is aging (56% weight remaining).
